candidates.summary: no test distinguishes crypto.AddressFromBech32 from the bech32.Decode it replaces, so reverting CreateUsernameFromBech32 leaves the whole gnoweb package green
candidates.failure_scenario: Revert CreateUsernameFromBech32 to its pre-PR body (bech32.Decode, truncate on success) and `go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/ -count=1` still reports ok. TestHTTPHandler_GetUserView_Address, the only test that touches the function, feeds it g1manfred47kzduec920z88wfr64ylksmdcedlf5, which both spellings truncate identically to g1ma...dlf5. The behaviour the PR actually buys — a bech32 string with a foreign HRP (cosmos1...) or a payload that is not 20 bytes is a name, not an address — is pinned by nothing, so the next edit of this function restores the old reading silently and /u/<foreign bech32> goes back to rendering a truncated address the handler never validated.
candidates.verify_by: in a scratch worktree at 876762bd, replace the crypto.AddressFromBech32 body with the bech32.Decode body (re-adding the tm2/pkg/bech32 import) and run `go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/ -count=1`: expect a failure from one of the PR's own tests, observe every one of them pass
candidates.evidence: baseline, unmutated head: `go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/ -count=1` -> `ok github.com/gnolang/gno/gno.land/pkg/gnoweb 6.769s`. With CreateUsernameFromBech32 reverted to bech32.Decode, the same command prints exactly one failure, and it is the test written for this finding: `--- FAIL: TestB1CreateUsernameFromBech32_OnlyGnoAddressesAreTruncated (0.00s)` / `FAIL github.com/gnolang/gno/gno.land/pkg/gnoweb 7.926s`. Not one of TestHTTPHandler_GetUserView_Address, _NotAUser, _RegisteredWithoutPackages, _RejectsInvalidNames, _LookupFailureIsNotA404 or TestRoutes goes red.

candidates.failure_scenario: Delete the three-line guard and `go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/ -count=1` is still ok, including the two tests that feed listPathsFunc a []string{""} to exercise it. weburl.Parse("") already fails — reURLPath is `^/[a-z0-9_/-]*$` (weburl/url.go:303) and does not match the empty string — so the loop already took the `continue` in the error branch. candidates.failure_scenario: rpcClient.ListPaths returns [""] for a package with no subpaths (client.go:231, strings.Split of an empty string). Three of its four consumers now drop that element — the new guard at :515, `paths[0] == ""` in GetPathsListView at :864, and `if p != ""` in realm_directory.go:104 — while the subpaths goroutine appends strings.TrimPrefix("", domain) into the overview's subpath list, so a leaf realm carries one empty subpath entry into the view. Pre-existing, and in scope because this diff sweeps that class and misses this member.

candidates.evidence: call sites read at head: handler_http.go:505 (guarded by the diff), :857 (guarded at :864), :1203 (unguarded, appends at :1211), realm_directory.go:99 (guarded at :104).

candidates.summary: the default branch of userExists, the one that rejects an unrecognised qeval payload, is executed by no test
candidates.failure_scenario: Every evalFunc the PR adds returns one of three shapes: `(nil *...UserData)\n(false bool)`, resolveNamePayload(true/false), or an error. None returns a payload whose last line is neither `(true bool)` nor `(false bool)`, so replacing the default branch with `return true, nil` leaves the suite green. That branch is the whole defence against a ResolveName signature change on r/sys/users: if it silently became `return true, nil`, every /u/<name> would resolve as an existing user and the gate the PR exists to add would be off, with no test saying so.
candidates.verify_by: replace the default branch body with `return true, nil` and run `go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/ -count=1`: expect a red test, observe ok
candidates.evidence: read of the five evalFunc stubs in handler_http_test.go (lines 2007-2017, 2050, 2073, 2096, 2135) plus MockClient.Eval and the stubClient default: no payload reaches the default branch.
